newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Sapura aborts UMW stake buy plan -report.
newsitem.headline: Sapura aborts UMW stake buy plan -report.

text.p: Malaysian telecommunications firm Sapura Holdings Sdn Bhd has aborted its proposal to buy a 30 percent stake in vehicle concern UMW Holdings Bhd, the national Bernama news agency said on Wednesday.

Bernama quoted a Sapura statement as saying that the company was aborting the plan in order to dispel "negative connotations" in the public eye from accusations made in the press about Sapura's intentions in the proposed deal.
Sapura's officials could not be immediately contacted for comment.
Sapura had submitted a proposal to buy the stake in UMW from state investment fund Permodalan Nasional Bhd, which holds 45 percent of UMW's equity.
But the plan met with resistance from senior UMW officials and PNB who said they were not consulted on the proposed sale. Their comments were widely publicised in the domestic press.

Sapura said it and its shareholders were labelled greedy and were also accused of intending to deprive Bumiputra (ethnic Malay) unit holders of Amanah Saham Nasional trust fund and other PNB unit trusts from benefiting from investments in a profitable company like UMW, Bernama said.

"On the contrary, Sapura has and will continue to be a champion and patron of Bumiputra entrepreneurs and corporations and has to date nurtured many a company which has become successful and listworthy," Sapura said.
PNB would also have received about 530 million cash from the sale, the Sapura statement said.

Sapura also said it had not lost interest in UMW. "This does in no manner negate our continued interest in acquiring the abovesaid equity if PNB wishes to in the future, divest the same be it upon the terms quoted above or such other terms as may mutually be agreed to," the statement said.

The company said its proposal to acquire UMW would have benefited PNB in many ways including a direct 30-40 percent stake in Sapura and indirect equity interest in three listed companies within the Sapura group.
These are publicly-traded Uniphone Telecommunications Bhd and Sapura Telecommunications Bhd, and soon-to-be-listed Sapura Motors Bhd, and UMW itself.

UMW makes light and heavy equipment for the industrial, construction and agricultural sectors. It also assembles and markets passenger and commercial vehicles, and is the Malaysian distributor of Japanese Toyota vehicles.
